question.text: Two resistances at $0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ with temperature coefficient of resistance $\alpha_{1}$ and $\alpha_{2}$ joined in series act as a single resistance in a circuit. The temperature coefficient of their single resistance will be

solution.text:
$\begin{aligned} R_{1} &=R_{0}\left(1+\alpha_{1} t\right)+R_{0}\left(1+\alpha_{2} t\right) \\ &=2 R_{0}\left(1+\frac{\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2}}{2} t\right) \end{aligned}$

Comparing with $R=R_{0}(1+\alpha t)$

$\alpha=\frac{\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2}}{2}$
